This is the "seed-library" analysis, which you tell me Pat made: three catalogue apps (kernelry, loamly, sprigg) compared on four criteria to answer "Which catalogue app should the Thornbury seed library adopt?". The stored record does not name an author, so I am relying on you for that. I only read it and changed nothing. The three findings that matter most for the steering group:

1. Yearly cost has no direction of preference. The stored criterion says `none`, so nobody can say whether cheaper or dearer is better, and the tool counts it as excluded from every dominance and ranking. The cost of the apps therefore plays no part in the comparison as it stands.
2. Two cells claim more than they show. Pat recorded confidence 3 (the top of that 1 to 3 scale) for kernelry/yearly-cost, which cites no evidence at all, and for loamly/volunteer-effort, which cites no primary or secondary source with a span to check. Loamly/ease-of-use is also thinly cited, but Pat recorded the lowest confidence (1) there, so that one is honest about its weakness.
3. Offline mode has no written definition, so it cannot be applied the same way twice. The tool lists it under criteria to redefine, and more evidence will not fix that.

One question for Pat, judged from the written definitions only and not from the correlation figures: volunteer effort is defined as "how many volunteer hours a week does running the app take, including learning it", and ease of use as "how quickly can a new volunteer learn to lend and return seed packets". Does volunteer effort count the same learning time that ease of use counts? If so, that learning time is weighted twice without anyone choosing it.

Where evidence for the two weak cells cannot be had, the honest recommendation is that Pat record a blank with the code that fits (`not-evidenced` if the sources are silent, `indeterminate` if they conflict) rather than keep a value that cannot be checked.

```
Uncited or thinly cited: kernelry/yearly-cost, loamly/volunteer-effort, loamly/ease-of-use
Rests on inference only: none
Confidence above its evidence: kernelry/yearly-cost, loamly/volunteer-effort
No direction of preference: yearly-cost
Overlap to put to the author: volunteer-effort + ease-of-use
Redefine: offline-mode
Changed: nothing
```
